item.title: PEI Envirothon: Becoming an Advisor
item.description:
PEI Envirothon: Becoming an Advisor kfarrar Mon, 10/19/2026 - 12:20

Why should I become a PEI Envirothon Advisor?

This program bridges the gap between the classroom and nature by bringing science and sustainability lessons into local forests, fields, and communities. Through hands-on outdoor learning, students deepen their understanding of ecology while building vital problem-solving skills for a more sustainable future. Team advisors help empower students to explore critical topics such as forestry, aquatics, wildlife and soils & land use through experiential learning and a team environment.

Envirothon takes learning beyond the classroom into the field and community, connecting students to the outdoors and building skills to solve real-world sustainability challenges.

What are the benefits of becoming a PEI Envirothon Advisor?

You will help guide students through inquiry-based learning aligned with science curricula across subjects like Environmental Science, Forestry, and Agriculture. Benefits include:

  • Working with motivated conservation-minded students.
  • Accessing professional workshops and resources.
  • Fostering critical thinking and teamwork skills for future careers in sectors such as resource management and research.

How do I find the time to become an advisor for my PEI Envirothon team?

Advisors guide and support while students take the lead. You can easily manage the commitment by co-advising with a colleague or engaging community volunteers. In fact, it's recommended to have at least two advisors per school. Advisors for PEI Envirothon teams could also be a parent or guardian. 

What supports or resources will be available to me?

Advisors receive comprehensive tools including study materials, virtual workshops, guest speaker connections, and hands-on field day opportunities.

The PEI Envirothon has provided ample study materials for each core topic that fall within the guidelines. Please click below to view the resources for each core topic (these will be updated periodically, as necessary):

  1. Forestry
  2. Aquatics and Water
  3. Wildlife and Habitats
  4. Soils and Land Use 

These resources are available online at any time. Additionally, advisors have found it useful to arrange to have guest speakers present to their class to discuss some of the more specialized areas of the program’s topics.

How do I get started as a PEI Envirothon Advisor? 

Join the network of educators shaping environmental education. Please work with your principal, or contact the PEI Envirothon Coordinator to learn more.

item.title: Opening doors, fostering futures during Foster Family Appreciation Week
item.description:
Opening doors, fostering futures during Foster Family Appreciation Week jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/19/2026 - 11:23

During Foster Family Appreciation Week, October 19-23, the province recognizes and celebrates the invaluable contributions of foster families across Prince Edward Island. 

Foster families play a special role in helping children and youth feel safe and cared for when they need it the most, a message reflected in the province’s Open Doors, Foster Futures recruitment campaign. By opening their hearts and homes, foster families help shape brighter futures while gaining meaningful and rewarding relationships of their own.

“Our government recognizes the deep compassion, dedication, and commitment it takes to be a foster family. Foster families provide children and youth in our province with safe, nurturing, and caring environments during challenging times. Their kindness and support make a lasting difference in the lives of young people and their families.”

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay 

The province is always looking for caring, compassionate, and skilled individuals and families who are willing to open their homes and make a meaningful difference in the lives of children and youth. Through its Open Doors, Foster Futures campaign, the province encourages more Islanders to learn about fostering and the positive impact they can have on a child’s future.

Those interested in fostering children and youth can attend an information session in Charlottetown or Summerside over the next three months.

For more information about becoming a foster parent in PEI, visit: Be a Foster Parent

item.title: October 19-23 is School Bus Safety Week
item.description:
October 19-23 is School Bus Safety Week jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/19/2026 - 10:18

The province is marking School Bus Safety Week by reminding Islanders to slow down, stay alert, and follow school bus laws to help protect students.

School Bus Safety Week serves as a timely reminder that everyone must work together to ensure students are kept safe when travelling to and from school each day.

“We all share a responsibility for keeping students safe on and around school buses. Drivers, parents, and students can all do their part by knowing the rules, staying alert, and remembering that no destination is worth putting someone’s safety at risk.”

- Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

Students should wait in a safe place away from the road and arrive at least five minutes early. They should follow the bus driver’s instructions, make sure the driver can see them, look both ways, and ensure the red lights are flashing before crossing in front of the bus.

Motorists should be aware of school buses and be prepared to stop when amber lights are flashing. When a school bus is stopped with its red-light flashing, drivers must stop at least six metres away and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.

 “We can never have too many reminders about staying safe on our roads," said Justice and Public Safety and Transportation and Infrastructure Minister Bloyce Thompson. "Slow down, look out for school buses, and never drive while distracted. Report any vehicle that illegally passes a school bus, and it will be investigated. Thank you to all the bus drivers, police officers, families, and responsible drivers for helping to protect students and making our roads safer."

It’s illegal and dangerous to pass a school bus when red lights are flashing. To protect Island students, drivers who illegally pass a school bus will lose their license and face a fine of up to $5,000.

Anyone who witnesses an incident while driving should pull over and call 9-1-1 to report. Note the license plate number, the vehicle and driver description, date and time of day, the location of the incident, and any other details that may assist the police.

Learn more at PrinceEdwardIsland.ca/SchoolBusSafety

item.title: Atlantic Fisheries Fund renewal brings $31.6 million investment in PEI over five years
item.description:
Atlantic Fisheries Fund renewal brings $31.6 million investment in PEI over five years jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/16/2026 - 15:24

The Atlantic provinces and the Government of Canada are renewing the Atlantic Fisheries Fund, investing an extra $31.6 million in Prince Edward Island's fisheries and aquaculture sector.

The investment includes $18.96 million in federal funding and $12.6 million in provincial funding. The Fund renewal reflects the ongoing partnership between Atlantic provinces and the federal government to make strategic investments that support industry priorities and create opportunities across the region and internationally.

"Prince Edward Island’s fisheries and aquaculture sector is a cornerstone of our economy and a vital source of jobs and opportunities across the province. This renewed agreement, which follows sustained advocacy by Atlantic Premiers with the Prime Minister, will help Island harvesters, processors, growers, and exporters invest in innovation, strengthen infrastructure and expand into new markets. As global demand continues to evolve, this investment will help ensure our seafood sector remains resilient, competitive, and positioned for long-term growth."

- Premier Rob Lantz

The original fund, signed in 2017, was designed to help the Atlantic region better meet growing market demand for sustainably sourced, high-quality fish and seafood. Over seven years, the fund supported 153 PEI-based projects and seven pan-Atlantic initiatives.    

The new Fund is based on the same three pillars including innovation, infrastructure, and science partnerships, with the addition of market diversification. Applicants can learn more and apply for support under any of the pillars by visiting the program webpage.

"Maintaining vibrant and prosperous fishing, aquaculture, and seafood industries is incredibly important for the communities that rely on them as well as the wider economy," said Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson. "A renewed Atlantic Fisheries Fund will support industry as it advances sustainable practices and ensures PEI's seafood sector remains strong and competitive for future generations. I'm particularly pleased with the new focus on market development and diversification as we work to expand opportunities for Island seafood in new and emerging markets."

Fisheries and aquaculture in Prince Edward Island have contributed approximately $400 million to the provincial economy and is three per cent of our provincial GDP. The industry is the economic driver in many rural communities, employing more than 5,000 people in peak season.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
